findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical sublinear balanced-BST solution: initialize lazy predecessor and successor stacks around the target, compare their nearest tops, and advance only the selected iterator k times. Both iterator transitions and exhaustion handling are explicit, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 272 and its Python TreeNode contract. The Reference preserves arbitrary output order, unique closest-set guarantee, both examples, all four constraints, and the balanced-tree sublinear follow-up; the contract now defines n and h.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064297956. Both sources have identical stack initialization boundaries, predecessor and successor advancement, distance comparison, k-step merge, and result; the only structural difference is the required local TreeNode equivalent versus LeetCode's injected model and wrapper.

The legal balanced 31/127/511-node tiers keep k = 8 and center the target between nearby values, exercising both lazy iterators while tree size grows. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent and 1.00x largest ratio; a correct full traversal and distance sort passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.68 relative exponent.

The Approach proves the two ordered stack-top invariant and now derives the amortized O(h + k) iterator bound, excludes returned values from O(h) auxiliary space, and explains exhausted-iterator and k = n behavior.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains source-fidelity verified with both examples, all four constraints, and the follow-up intact. Its one source tree image is now represented by one accessible Mermaid tree with matching nodes and edges and passes the Mermaid gate.
